terms.meaning: ordering items by their numeric score, here from high to low

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and status list
sections.what: Imports the screen parts, the storage helpers, and the status list.
sections.why: The status list is shared with the data file so names match.

sections.name: ApplicationsPage (part 1)
sections.title: Loading, sorting, and the page header
sections.what: Loads applications when the page opens and refreshes them on data changes. Sorts them by score and shows the title, count, and ingest button.
sections.why: Refreshing on the data-change event keeps the list current when another part of the app saves.
sections.watch_out: If a score is missing, the sort subtraction gives an unusable result and the order becomes unpredictable.

sections.name: ApplicationsPage (part 2)
sections.title: Table header row
sections.what: Draws the header row with columns for company, role, location, bucket, score, and status.
sections.why: Matches the columns the rows are meant to show.
sections.watch_out: The row contents were not in the reviewed section, so they are unverified.

summary: The list screen that shows every saved application sorted by score, with a button to add a new job.
purpose: Gives an overview of the whole job pipeline.
why: Likely reason: a sorted table lets the user scan which jobs to pursue first. The code does not state this.
how: On load, reads applications from storage and sorts them from highest to lowest score. Listens for data-change events to refresh. Shows a count, a table header, and an ingest button.
inputs: Saved applications from storage and data-change events.
outputs: A table of applications and a total count, plus navigation links.
risks: Only the header and setup were reviewed, so the table rows are not verified. The first draw happens before storage is read, so the count shows zero briefly.
debug: If the list is empty, check the applications key in browser storage. If the list does not update after a save, check that the data-change event fires.
